question: Should OpenClaw standardize these five public memory-role slots, the legacy `memory`-to-`memory.recall` alias, and memory-only per-agent overrides as the initial contract?
rationale: The proposal defines durable configuration, migration, and plugin API semantics; repository evidence can validate feasibility but cannot choose the permanent role taxonomy or ownership boundary.

options.title: Sponsor the five-role contract
options.body: Accept the proposed taxonomy after assigning a unique RFC number, refreshing exact-head proof, and completing the RFC lifecycle metadata.

options.title: Narrow the first phase
options.body: Standardize only immediately proven roles such as recall and capture, leaving compaction, dreaming, and user-model ownership for follow-up RFCs.

options.title: Defer the public contract
options.body: Keep the RFC in draft until memory orchestration and plugin ownership requirements stabilize further.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the five-role contract
recommendation.body: Accept the proposed taxonomy after assigning a unique RFC number, refreshing exact-head proof, and completing the RFC lifecycle metadata.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged-history work is most directly connected to the proposed slot API, agent overrides, and compatibility semantics.
